body:
## Why

`packages/fleet/lib/review-runner.mjs` builds the review subprocess environment as:

```js
const env = { ...process.env, PATH: safePath };
```

Only `PATH` is sanitized. Every other ambient variable is passed straight through — including the ADLC ledger signing key.

**The asymmetry is the defect.** `modelPlaneEnv()` maintains a `NEVER_EXEMPT` set for one stated reason: a process holding that key could forge the `cross-model-review` attestations the trust-root merge gate is built on. There is a comment saying exactly that, and the build worker is scrubbed accordingly and correctly never receives it.

The **prosecutor** is not scrubbed at all. So the process whose verdict the merge gate trusts is the one running with the credential that could forge that verdict.

This is defence-in-depth rather than an active leak — `adversarial-review` is deliberately resolved to a trusted absolute binary (L1/M2), and it sends the diff to a provider, not the environment. But "no legitimate reason to hold it" is the entire basis of `NEVER_EXEMPT`, and the reviewer has none.

**Found by** an adversarial-review round on the #396 branch. The finding as reported claimed reviewer-group members were dispatched without transport credential selection; that mechanism does not exist (fleet never adapter-dispatches reviewer members). Verifying the claim surfaced this instead.

## What to build

**1. Deny the never-exempt set from the review subprocess.**

The child environment excludes every name in `NEVER_EXEMPT`. Scoped precisely to that set — the fix is NOT `modelPlaneEnv` as-is, because the reviewer legitimately needs provider API keys to call a model, and stripping them would break every review.

**2. Make the environment source injectable**, the way `spawn`, `trustedPath` and `resolveBin` already are in this module. A test must be able to assert on the env the runner actually passes to `spawn` without mutating the real `process.env` of the test runner, which is shared mutable state across a parallel suite.

**3. Do not broaden the scrub in this ticket.** Deciding which provider credentials a reviewer *should* see is a separate question, and containment of the model plane generally is #395. This ticket closes exactly one hole: the key that can forge the evidence.

### Binding rules

- **`NEVER_EXEMPT` stays the single source of truth.** The review runner must read that set, not restate its members — a second copy is a second thing to forget when the set grows.
- **A review that works today still works.** Provider credentials continue to reach the reviewer untouched.
- **`PATH` sanitation is unchanged.** The existing L1/M2 trusted-binary resolution is orthogonal and must not regress.

## Acceptance criteria

- The environment the review runner passes to `spawn` contains NO name in `NEVER_EXEMPT`, asserted against the real exported set rather than a hard-coded string, so a future addition to that set is covered without editing the test. Verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/review-runner-env.test.mjs`.
- Provider credentials still reach the reviewer: an env carrying `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY` and `GEMINI_API_KEY` arrives at `spawn` with all three intact and their values unchanged. Verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/review-runner-env.test.mjs`.
- The scrub is driven through the REAL `makeReviewRunner` with an injected `spawn`, never a re-implementation of its env construction — a copy of the logic under test cannot catch drift in the thing it copies. Verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/review-runner-env.test.mjs`.
- `PATH` is still sanitized to absolute, non-worktree directories, and the value the child receives is the sanitized one, not the ambient one. Verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/review-runner-env.test.mjs`.
- The runner never mutates the environment object it was handed: the source object is byte-identical before and after a review, so a caller passing `process.env` cannot have the host environment altered underneath it. Verified by `node --test packages/fleet/test/review-runner-env.test.mjs`.
- Every existing review-runner behaviour is unchanged — trusted-binary resolution, `--base`/`--json` argv, exit-code handling, and the fail-closed paths all still pass: `node --test packages/fleet/test/live-prosecute.test.mjs` exits 0.
- Every affected segment is green: `node scripts/run-tests.mjs` exits 0, and the diff-scoped mutation gate reports no survivor: `node scripts/mutation-gate.mjs origin/main --max 12` exits 0.

## Context

- Issue #446.
- Code: `packages/fleet/lib/review-runner.mjs` (env construction, `makeReviewRunner`), `packages/fleet/lib/env-scrub.mjs` (`NEVER_EXEMPT`, and the comment stating why it exists), `packages/fleet/lib/live-deps.mjs` (the one production caller).
- Existing coverage to extend rather than duplicate: `packages/fleet/test/live-prosecute.test.mjs` already drives `makeReviewRunner` with an injected `spawn` and captures the options object.
- Related and NOT in scope: #395 (model-plane workers run unsandboxed as the operator) — that governs containment once a process is running; this governs one credential it should never have been given.
- No rails are declared. "Existing review-runner behaviour is unchanged" and "`NEVER_EXEMPT` stays the single source of truth" are acceptance criteria instead, so this ticket cannot freeze a file for every other PR in the repo the way T151's rails did (#443 needed an admin override to expire them).
title: Deny the never-exempt ledger signing key from the review subprocess (#446)
